mainTopic: The חגיגה brought with the קרבן פסח on the 14th of ניסן: why it is optional, and how far בן תימא compares it to the פסח (eating time, roasting, which animal, and breaking bones)
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב אשי's point: the חגיגה brought with the פסח on the 14th of ניסן is not a Torah obligation. The proof is that it is not brought on שבת, in טומאה, or when there is plenty of פסח meat. It is brought when the meat is small, so that the פסח can be eaten על השבע, when one is already full. The גמרא then notes that the משנה, which lets this חגיגה be eaten for two days, does not follow בן תימא. בן תימא treats it like the פסח and allows only a day and a night, based on the פסוק 'ולא ילין לבקר זבח חג הפסח'. The גמרא asks how far this comparison goes, and proves that for בן תימא the חגיגה must also be roasted. It must also come only from a male, one-year-old sheep or goat, like the פסח. Finally it asks whether breaking a bone of this חגיגה is forbidden. It tries to prove this from a משנה about a knife and a cleaver found in Jerusalem. The proof is pushed off by setting the case on שבת, that reading is refuted from the סיפא, and a new answer begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Fourteenth's Festival Offering Is Not an Obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes from the משנה's limits that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר is not a חובה. If it were, it would be brought on שבת, with a large amount of meat, and in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not an obligation. For if you thought it was an obligation, it should be brought on שבת, and when there is a lot of meat, and in a state of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב אשי's inference, which began on the previous page. Because the משנה asks 'when does one bring a חגיגה with the פסח?', this חגיגה must be optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows this חגיגה only on a weekday, in טהרה, and when the פסח meat is small (מועט). Real communal obligations override שבת and טומאה, and they do not depend on how much food there is. So the conditions in the משנה show that this offering is not a חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligation required by the Torah
For if it should enter your mind (introduces a rejected assumption)
A large amount (of פסח meat per person)
Ritual impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic status of the חגיגת ארבעה עשר. Because it is voluntary, the next step must explain why it is brought at all.

phrases.english: is not an obligation.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב אשי's statement that started on 69b: 'the חגיגה of the fourteenth...'

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind that it is an obligation —
it should come on Shabbat,
and it should come when the portion is large,
and it should come in a state of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו חוֹבָה הִיא. דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חוֹבָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's inference from the משנה's wording 'אימתי מביא' (earlier).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חגיגת ארבעה עשר is not a Torah obligation, because the משנה limits it to a weekday, טהרה, and a small amount of meat.

steps.title: Why Bring It at All When the Meat Is Small?
steps.stepSummary: If the offering is optional, why is it brought in the case of a small amount of meat?
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the small-amount case, what is the reason it is brought?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If this חגיגה is not required, what purpose does it serve in the מועט case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed the offering is optional. Yet the משנה still says to bring it when the פסח meat is small. The גמרא wants the reason behind that practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A small amount (of פסח meat per person)
However / in any case
What is the reason?

phrases.english: But with a small amount, in any case,
what is the reason it comes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the offering is optional and asks for its purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason an optional חגיגה is brought when the פסח meat is small.

steps.title: So the פסח Is Eaten When Already Full
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חגיגה is eaten first, so that the פסח will be eaten על השבע (when one is already satisfied).
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the חגיגה that comes with the פסח is eaten first, so that the פסח will be eaten when one is full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The חגיגה is food eaten first, so that people reach the פסח already full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the פסח meat is small, people would come to it hungry. The חגיגה fills them up first, so the פסח is eaten in a dignified, satisfied way. When there is plenty of פסח meat, this need does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Festival peace-offering (שלמים)
When already satiated / full

steps.whatToRemember: The חגיגת ארבעה עשר is optional. It is brought when the פסח meat is small, so that the פסח can be eaten על השבע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea of eating the פסח (and today the אפיקומן) when already full.

phrases.english: As it was taught: The Festival offering that comes with the Paschal lamb
is eaten first,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא פֶּסַח נֶאֱכָל עַל הַשָּׂבָע.
phrases.english: so that the Paschal lamb will be eaten when one is satiated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: חֲגִיגָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַפֶּסַח נֶאֱכֶלֶת תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is eaten first so the פסח is eaten על השבע, which is needed only when the פסח meat is small.

steps.title: The משנה Does Not Follow בן תימא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the חגיגה is eaten for two days and notes that this rule disagrees with בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it is eaten for two days, etc.' Our משנה is not like בן תימא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It notes which תנא does not agree with it, which sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the חגיגת ארבעה עשר like ordinary שלמים, eaten for two days and one night. The גמרא flags that בן תימא held otherwise. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues)
Our משנה
Not in accordance with

phrases.english: 'And it is eaten for two days, etc.'
Our mishna is not in accordance with ben Teima.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how long the חגיגה may be eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's two-day eating period for the חגיגת ארבעה עשר disagrees with בן תימא.

steps.title: בן תימא: The Fourteenth's Offering Is Like the פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes בן תימא: the חגיגה brought with the פסח is like the פסח and is eaten for only a day and a night. The חגיגה of the fifteenth is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, בן תימא says: the חגיגה that comes with the פסח is like the פסח, and it is eaten only for a day and a night. But the חגיגה of the fifteenth is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves בן תימא disagrees with the משנה. It shows his different time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן תימא links the 14th's חגיגה to the פסח it accompanies, so it gets the פסח's short eating time. The 15th's חגיגה is a regular festival שלמים, so it gets the normal two days and one night. The משנה gives the 14th's חגיגה two days, so the two clearly disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like the פסח (gets its laws)
For a day and a night

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two חגיגות. 'חגיגת ארבעה עשר' is the optional one brought with the פסח on the 14th. 'חגיגת חמשה עשר' is the regular festival offering on the first day of יום טוב.

phrases.english: For it was taught, ben Teima says:
The Festival offering that comes with the Paschal lamb
is like the Paschal lamb,
and is eaten only for a day and a night.
And the Festival offering of the fifteenth —
is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow בן תימא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which בן תימא limits the 14th's חגיגה to a day and a night.

steps.title: The Fourteenth's Offering Counts for שמחה, Not for חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: an animal set aside as the חגיגת ארבעה עשר can fulfill the מצוה of שמחה, but not the obligation of the festival חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with the חגיגה of the fourteenth, one fulfills the obligation of rejoicing, but one does not fulfill the obligation of the festival offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a further rule about the 14th's offering. It can be used for the מצוה of שמחה on the festival, but it does not count as one's חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose one set aside an animal for the 14th and did not offer it then, so it was brought on the 15th. It can still satisfy שמחה (eating festive שלמים). It cannot replace the required festival חגיגה. The גמרא does not explain this rule. The next step instead asks for the source of בן תימא's main ruling, the day-and-night time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: One fulfills (an obligation) with it
The מצוה of festival rejoicing (eating שלמים)
The חגיגה brought with the פסח on the 14th

steps.whatToRemember: בן תימא: the 14th's חגיגה is eaten like the פסח (a day and a night). It can count toward שמחה, but not toward the festival חגיגה obligation.

phrases.english: And the Festival offering of the fourteenth —
one fulfills with it the obligation of rejoicing,
but one does not fulfill with it the obligation of the Festival offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲגִיגַת אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹצֵא בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of בן תימא with an added ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal of the חגיגת ארבעה עשר fulfills שמחה but not the festival חגיגה obligation.

steps.title: What is the source for בן תימא's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and Torah source behind בן תימא's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for בן תימא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בן תימא holds that the חגיגה brought with the פסח may be eaten only for one day and one night. This question sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שלמים can be eaten for two days and one night. בן תימא gives this חגיגה the shorter time limit of the פסח, so the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (a request for the source or logic)

phrases.english: What is the reason of ben Teima?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the בן תימא ruling quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind בן תימא's rule that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר may only be eaten for one day and one night.

steps.title: One verse covers both the חגיגה and the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב taught that the verse 'זבח חג הפסח' refers to both the חגיגה and the פסח, and the Torah says neither may be left until morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב taught his son חייא: 'Neither shall the offering of the feast of the Passover be left until morning.' 'The offering of the feast' refers to the חגיגה. 'The Passover' means what it says, the פסח itself. And the Torah says about both: 'It shall not be left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is a פסוק. רב reads that פסוק as speaking about two different קרבנות at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זבח חג' are read as the חגיגה, and 'הפסח' as the פסח. One command, 'לא ילין,' then applies to both. So the חגיגה, like the פסח, must be finished before morning.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be left overnight until morning
The offering of the festival, read here as the חגיגה
According to its plain meaning
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison (היקש) between the חגיגה and the פסח is the base for all the questions that follow. Each one asks how far the comparison goes.

phrases.english: As Rav taught to Ḥiyya his son:
"Neither shall be left until the morning
the offering of the feast of the Passover",
"the offering of the feast": this is the Festival peace-offering,
"the Passover": as it sounds (the Paschal lamb),
and the Merciful One said: "It shall not be left over."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ולא ילין לבקר זבח חג הפסח' joins the חגיגה to the פסח, so the חגיגה may not be left until morning.

steps.title: Must בן תימא's חגיגה also be roasted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the comparison to the פסח applies only to the time limit or also to the rule of roasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to בן תימא, is the חגיגה eaten roasted or not? When the Torah compared it to the פסח, was that only about leaving it overnight, but not about roasting? Or perhaps there is no difference, and it must be roasted too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that builds on the verse it just explained. It wants to know whether the חגיגה must be roasted, just like the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Maybe the verse only compares the two קרבנות for the one rule it mentions, 'לא ילין.' Or maybe the comparison is complete, so every rule of the פסח, including roasting, applies to the חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open question)
Roasted over fire
Compared it (made a היקש)
Leaving overnight
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
According to ben Teima, is it eaten roasted
or is it not eaten roasted?
When the Merciful One compared it to the Paschal lamb, was it for leaving overnight,
but for roasting, no,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְבֶן תֵּימָא נֶאֱכֶלֶת צָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the comparison from step 8 and asks how far it extends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the comparison between the חגיגה and the פסח also requires the חגיגה to be roasted.

steps.title: Proof from 'tonight it is all roasted'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה of מה נשתנה says that on this night all the meat is roasted, and רב חסדא says this follows בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'On this night it is all roasted.' And רב חסדא said: this is the opinion of בן תימא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof to answer the question about roasting. It quotes the משנה of the questions asked on ליל הסדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'all' the meat eaten that night is roasted. That includes the חגיגה eaten alongside the פסח. רב חסדא says this follows בן תימא, which shows that בן תימא requires the חגיגה to be roasted too.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it is roasted

steps.confusionAlert: The proof works because of the word 'כולו' (all). If only the פסח were roasted and the חגיגה were cooked another way, the meat of that night would not be 'all roasted.'

phrases.english: Come and hear:
On this night it is all roasted.
And Rav Ḥisda said:
This is the statement of ben Teima.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה כּוּלּוֹ צָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That according to בן תימא the חגיגת ארבעה עשר must be roasted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of מה נשתנה ('הלילה הזה כולו צלי'), which רב חסדא says follows בן תימא.

steps.title: Conclusion: the חגיגה must be roasted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that according to בן תימא, the חגיגה must be roasted like the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question about roasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בן תימא, the comparison between the חגיגה and the פסח is not limited to the overnight rule. It also covers roasting.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: For בן תימא, the חגיגת ארבעה עשר is compared to the פסח in two ways. It may be eaten only for one day and one night, and it must be roasted.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to בן תימא, the חגיגת ארבעה עשר is eaten roasted.

steps.title: Does the חגיגה share the פסח's animal rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to בן תימא, the חגיגה may come from cattle, from females, or from a two-year-old animal, all of which are not allowed for a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked according to בן תימא: may it come from cattle or not? May it come from females or not? May it come from a two-year-old animal or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new set of questions. It asks whether the comparison to the פסח also limits which animals can be used for the חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be a male sheep or goat in its first year. A normal שלמים can be from cattle, male or female, and older. The question is whether בן תימא's comparison brings these limits of the פסח onto the חגיגה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Cattle (the herd), as opposed to sheep and goats
Female animals
A two-year-old animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the roasting question. Roasting is about how the meat is eaten. This question is about which animal may be used in the first place.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them according to ben Teima:
Does it come from the herd (cattle)
or does it not come from the herd,
does it come from females
or does it not come from females,
does it come as a two-year-old

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינָהּ בָּאָה בַּת שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים?
phrases.english: or does it not come as a two-year-old?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ לְבֶן תֵּימָא: בָּאָה מִן הַבָּקָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that the comparison covers roasting, the גמרא asks whether it also covers the rules about which animals may be used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to בן תימא, the חגיגת ארבעה עשר follows the פסח's limits: only sheep or goats, only males, and only in the first year.

steps.title: The root of the question: eating rules only, or everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the logic behind the question from Step 12. When the Torah compared the חגיגה to the פסח, was it only about eating, or about every detail?
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah compared the חגיגה to the פסח, maybe it was only for matters of eating, but not for everything. Or maybe there is no difference, and it applies to everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the two sides of the question it just asked about cattle, females, and two-year-old animals. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know (Steps 8–11) that the חגיגה shares the פסח's eating rules: the time limit and roasting. The open question is whether the comparison stops there or also covers the rules about which animal may be brought. Side one says: eating only. Side two says: no difference, everything.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (the Merciful One) compared it
Matters of eating
For all matters
There is no difference

phrases.english: When the Merciful One compared it to the Paschal offering —
phrases.notes: This refers to the verse ״זבח חג הפסח״ from Step 8.

phrases.english: was it for matters of eating,
but for all other matters — not,
or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question asked in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the comparison between the חגיגה and the פסח cover only eating rules, or every rule?

steps.title: A ברייתא: the חגיגה is like the פסח in every detail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing all the ways the חגיגה brought with the פסח matches the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the חגיגה that comes with the פסח is just like the פסח. It comes from sheep or goats, not cattle. It comes from males, not females. It comes from a one-year-old animal, not a two-year-old. It is eaten only for a day and a night, only roasted, and only by those who signed up for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching (ברייתא) that answers the question directly. It lists every way the חגיגה is like the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list includes the animal rules: flock not herd, male not female, and one year old not two. These are not eating rules. So the ברייתא seems to say the comparison covers everything. It also repeats the eating rules: a day and a night, roasted, and only for those signed up.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival offering brought together with the פסח on the 14th of ניסן
Flock (sheep and goats) / herd (cattle)
Within its first year
Those registered for it in advance

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: חֲגִיגָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַפֶּסַח
phrases.english: Come and hear: the festival offering that comes with the Paschal offering
is like the Paschal offering:
it comes from the flock
and does not come from the herd,
it comes from males
and does not come from females,
it comes as a one-year-old
and does not come as a two-year-old,
and it is eaten only for a day and a night,
and it is eaten only roasted,
and it is eaten only by those registered for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the חגיגה matches the פסח in all matters, not just eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing all the ways the חגיגה matches the פסח.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows בן תימא, so the comparison is total
steps.stepSummary: Only בן תימא holds that the חגיגה is compared to the פסח, so the ברייתא is his. Therefore, by his view, the חגיגה matches the פסח in everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who do we know holds this idea? בן תימא. Learn from this that we require all the details. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose view the ברייתא reflects. It then closes the question: according to בן תימא, every rule of the פסח applies to this חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could be used as proof only if it matches בן תימא's opinion. Since he is the one who compares the חגיגה to the פסח (Steps 5 and 8), the ברייתא must be his. That settles it: the animal-type rules apply too, not just the eating rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Who have you heard holds this?
This line of reasoning
Learn from it (a proof is accepted)
We require all the details

steps.whatToRemember: According to בן תימא, the חגיגה of the 14th of ניסן is like the פסח in every way. It must be a male, one-year-old sheep or goat, eaten roasted within a day and a night, and only by those registered for it.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִית לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא — בֶּן תֵּימָא,
phrases.english: who holds this reasoning? Ben Teima.
Learn from this that we require all the details.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to בן תימא, the חגיגה is fully compared to the פסח: no cattle, no females, and no two-year-olds.

steps.title: Does the ban on breaking a bone apply to the חגיגה?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: according to בן תימא, is it forbidden to break a bone of the חגיגה, as it is with the פסח? The word ״בּוֹ״ ("in it") might exclude the חגיגה, or it might only exclude a disqualified פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to בן תימא, does the חגיגה have the ban on breaking a bone, or not? Maybe, even though the Torah compared it to the פסח, the verse says ״בּוֹ״, "in it": in the פסח and not in the חגיגה. Or maybe this word ״בּוֹ״ comes to teach that the ban applies to a valid פסח and not a disqualified one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about one more rule of the פסח: the ban on breaking its bones. It lays out two possible ways to read the word ״בּוֹ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the comparison is total, so you might expect the bone ban to apply too. But the verse ״ועצם לא תשברו בו״ says ״בּוֹ״, "in it". Side one reads ״בּוֹ״ as "only the פסח, not the חגיגה", which would override the comparison. Side two says ״בּוֹ״ is needed for a different lesson (a valid פסח, not a disqualified one), so the חגיגה would still be included.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Breaking a bone (forbidden for the פסח)
"In it": a limiting word in the verse
Valid / disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings of ״בּוֹ״. In side one, ״בּוֹ״ means "not the חגיגה". In side two, ״בּוֹ״ means "not a disqualified פסח", so it says nothing against the חגיגה. The word can only be used for one lesson.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised to them according to Ben Teima:
is it subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם?
phrases.english: or is it not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי אַקְּשֵׁיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְפֶסַח,
phrases.english: Even though the Merciful One compared it to the Paschal offering,
the verse says "in it."
phrases.notes: This refers to Exodus 12:46: "and you shall not break a bone in it".

phrases.english: "In it" — and not in the festival offering.
Or perhaps this "in it" —
comes to teach: a valid one and not a disqualified one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the comparison is total and asks whether the word ״בּוֹ״ excludes the חגיגה from the bone ban.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to בן תימא, does the ban on breaking a bone apply to the חגיגה, or does ״בּוֹ״ exclude it?

steps.title: A knife and a cleaver found in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A slaughtering knife found on the 14th of ניסן may be used right away. One found on the 13th must be immersed again. A cleaver must be immersed again on either day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A knife found on the 14th: you may slaughter with it right away. Found on the 13th: you immerse it again. A cleaver, whether found on this day or that day: you immerse it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to try to answer the question about breaking a bone of the חגיגה. This step only presents the source; the next steps show how it might prove something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 14th we assume a lost slaughtering knife was already immersed, because everyone purifies their knives on the 13th to slaughter the פסח. A cleaver is used for chopping bones. The משנה says we do not make that assumption for a cleaver, even on the 14th. The גמרא will ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: a slaughtering knife
a cleaver, a heavy knife used to chop bones
he immerses it again, to make it טהור

steps.confusionAlert: The two knives get different rulings only on the 14th. On the 13th, both must be immersed again. The whole proof depends on why the cleaver is not trusted on the 14th.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A knife that was found on the fourteenth (of Nisan)
one may slaughter with it immediately.
phrases.notes: We assume it was already immersed on the 13th, in preparation for the פסח.

phrases.english: On the thirteenth, he must immerse it again.
phrases.notes: Perhaps its owner had not yet immersed it.

phrases.english: A cleaver, whether on this day or on that day
he must immerse it again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question raised in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the חגיגה has a prohibition of breaking a bone according to בן תימא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a knife and a cleaver found on the 13th or 14th of ניסן

steps.title: The משנה cannot follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows. If it is the רבנן, the cleaver should also be presumed immersed on the 14th, since it is needed for chopping the bones of the חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say the רבנן: why is the knife different, that we assume it was immersed? Because it is fit for the פסח. Then a cleaver too is fit for the חגיגה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests whether the משנה could follow the רבנן and shows a difficulty. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not compare the חגיגה to the פסח, so they allow its bones to be broken. Then people would also immerse their cleavers before the 14th, to chop the חגיגה bones. So a cleaver found on the 14th should be trusted just like the knife, but the משנה says it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
If you say...
What is the difference?
it is fit or usable for

phrases.english: Whose view is it? If you say the Rabbis,
what is different about a knife, that he immerses it (on the 13th)?
Because it is fit for the Paschal lamb.
A cleaver too: it is fit for the Festival offering!
phrases.notes: According to the רבנן, the חגיגה's bones may be broken, so a cleaver would be needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה from Step 17 to find whose view it follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying that the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חגיגה's bones may be broken, a cleaver is needed on the 14th and would be immersed in advance like the knife. The משנה's ruling then makes no sense.

steps.title: So the משנה is בן תימא, and the חגיגה has a bone prohibition
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה must follow בן תימא. This proves that, in his view, the חגיגה also has the prohibition of breaking a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not בן תימא's view? And learn from it that the prohibition of breaking a bone applies to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its proof. The משנה follows בן תימא, and he forbids breaking the bones of the חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no bones may be broken on the 14th, of either the פסח or the חגיגה, nobody needs a cleaver that day. So there is no reason to assume a cleaver was immersed. This explains the משנה and answers the question from Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...?
Learn from it: a proven conclusion
breaking a bone, forbidden for the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: Rather, is it not ben Teima's view?
And learn from it
that the prohibition of breaking a bone applies to it (the Festival offering).
phrases.notes: So no cleaver is needed on the 14th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the רבנן cannot explain the משנה (Step 18), it must be בן תימא.
steps.raayaObject: For בן תימא, breaking a bone of the חגיגה is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that a cleaver must always be immersed again

steps.title: No: the משנה can follow the רבנן when the 14th falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה can follow the רבנן if the 14th fell on שבת. Then no חגיגה is brought, so no cleaver is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It really is the רבנן, and the case is where the 14th falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. It shows that the משנה can fit the רבנן after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the 14th is on שבת, everyone agrees the חגיגה is not offered. So no one needs a cleaver that day, and there is no reason to assume it was immersed. The next step challenges this answer from the סיפא of the same משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really: the original option still stands
and the case is, for example, where...
שבת, when the חגיגה of the 14th is not brought

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tries to deflect the cleaver proof by setting the משנה on a שבת, when no חגיגה is brought. Steps 21–22 show that this exact reading fails, and the גמרא then begins a different reading.
steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not say the רבנן forbid breaking the חגיגה's bones. It says that on this particular day there is simply no חגיגה, so a cleaver is not needed.

phrases.english: No, it is actually the Rabbis,
and the case is where it (the 14th) came on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: On שבת the חגיגה of the 14th is not offered, so a cleaver is not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 19 by reading the משנה as a specific case that fits the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, but does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the cleaver would be needed for a חגיגה on the 14th. If the 14th falls on שבת, there is no חגיגה, so even the רבנן agree the cleaver is not trusted.

steps.title: The later clause of the משנה already covers שבת, so the first clause cannot be about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 20. The סיפא of the משנה deals with a 14th that fell on שבת as its own case. This shows the רישא is not about שבת. So the claim 'the 14th fell on שבת, so no חגיגה' cannot explain the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the later part of the משנה teaches: If the 14th fell on שבת, he may slaughter with the knife right away. If it is found on the 15th, he may slaughter with it right away. If a cleaver was found tied to the knife, it is treated just like the knife. From this we learn that the first part of the משנה is not talking about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back against the answer it just gave in Step 20. That answer said the משנה is talking about a year when the 14th fell on שבת. The גמרא shows from the rest of the משנה that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא gives the case of '14th on שבת' its own, different ruling: the knife may be used right away. If the רישא were also about שבת, the משנה could not give it a different ruling (immerse again). So the רישא must be about a regular weekday. On a weekday a חגיגה is brought, so according to the רבנן the cleaver should be presumed immersed, and the question from Step 18 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The later (closing) part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first (opening) part of a משנה or ברייתא
A cleaver, a heavy knife used for chopping bones
By inference, we can learn from this that
We are dealing with (this case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts of the משנה. The סיפא is the part that talks about שבת. The point is that because the סיפא mentions שבת on its own, the רישא must be about an ordinary weekday.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings back the proof that the משנה follows בן תימא. If the רישא is about a weekday, the רבנן should treat the cleaver as immersed. The question of Step 18 is open again.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
phrases.notes: This opens a challenge using the rest of the same משנה.

phrases.notes: Knives cannot be immersed on שבת, so it was surely immersed before שבת.

and on the fifteenth
phrases.notes: The first day of the Festival.

phrases.english: he may slaughter with it immediately.
phrases.notes: It was surely immersed the day before.

phrases.english: If a cleaver was found tied to a knife
it is like the knife.
By inference, that in the first clause
phrases.notes: This is the conclusion the גמרא draws from the סיפא.

phrases.english: we are not dealing with Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the rejection in Step 20, which set the משנה on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 20 that the רישא of the משנה is about a 14th that fell on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא lists 'the 14th fell on שבת' as its own case. That means the רישא must be about a weekday. On a weekday a חגיגה is brought, so the answer from Step 20 fails.

steps.title: A new answer begins: the case is one where the פסח came in a special way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'שבת' answer. It starts a new explanation of the רישא: a case where the פסח 'came' in some special way. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where [the פסח] came...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It drops the שבת answer and begins a different explanation for why no cleaver would be needed even according to the רבנן. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ואלא' tells us the previous answer has been abandoned. The גמרא will now describe a different weekday situation where no חגיגה is brought with the פסח. If that works, the רישא can still follow the רבנן, and the proof for בן תימא is rejected again.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the previous answer and offer a new one)
That it came (describing how the פסח was brought)

phrases.english: Rather, [it is a case] where it came
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 21 knocked down the שבת answer, this begins a different answer to the question of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (אוקימתא) so that no חגיגה is brought, even on a weekday.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רישא is about a weekday, a חגיגה is brought. So the רבנן should treat the cleaver as immersed, which means the משנה must follow בן תימא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to be completed on the next amud: a special way the פסח was brought, with no חגיגה, so the משנה can follow the רבנן.
